text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today, essentially flat, after oil prices dropped on news of a potential Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire declaration. Crude oil has been volatile over recent weeks amid geopolitical tensions—world oil was trading at $125 per barrel today versus $96 for U.S. crude—and the prospect of reduced conflict and energy disruption typically weighs on oil prices, which in turn pressures the stock of a major oil producer.

The stock has still climbed 5.3% over two weeks, reflecting the broader strength in oil markets as investors priced in supply concerns from Middle East tensions and sanctions dynamics. Today's small decline appears to be a pullback within that rally rather than a reversal, as ceasefire talk creates uncertainty about whether geopolitical risk premiums will hold.
